raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Wan-Animate-2's in-context self-attention is about 71% of GPU time per denoising step on H100 (torch profiler). It runs compiled flex_attention over a padded [generation | reference video] layout that is always sized for a full-length clip, so short clips also pay for the padded frames.

## Modifications

1. **Exact FA3 path for the in-context attention (Hopper).** `_in_context_attention` computes the same masked attention as FA3 calls merged by log-sum-exp with the existing `merge_state` kernel:
   - dense FA3 over the generation keys;
   - varlen FA3 per frame over the reference keys (generation frame j attends reference frame j-1);
   - for `log_scale != 0` (distilled checkpoint), generation frame 1's keys get their own call with `lse + log_scale`, which equals the score bias;
   - a short clip's missing frames are zero keys under the full-clip mask, so they are added back exactly as `out * sigmoid(lse - log(num_zero_keys))`.

   `_split_attention_is_exact` gates it. Grids that differ by a row, batch > 1 and non-Hopper GPUs keep the flex path unchanged.
2. **Opt-in FP8 reference K/V cache.** `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_WAN_ANIMATE_2_FP8_REFERENCE_KV=1` (default off) stores the per-clip reference K/V as `float8_e4m3fn` with one fp32 scale per (token, head). Each block dequantizes into its attention input. It errors on non-CUDA, below sm89, and ROCm.
3. The reference cache is stored once per clip in the padded slot layout, sized to that clip.

## Benchmark

H100 80GB, official Wan2.2 demo inputs (`examples/wan_animate/animate`), 944x528, seed 42, layerwise DiT offload and text encoder CPU offload as in CI, FP8 off unless noted. Single runs; the PR ran first on a cold compile cache. Denoise step = steady-state s/it.

| setting | main step | PR step | step speedup | end to end (main to PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, 1 GPU, 1 short clip, 40 steps | 9.75 s | 5.52 s | **1.77x** | 441.4 to 265.5 s (1.66x) |
| base, 1 GPU, 3 clips (2 full + short), 40 steps | 11.26 s (full clip) | 8.08 s | 1.39x (full), 3.17x (short) | 1299.6 to 809.5 s (**1.61x**) |
| distilled, 1 GPU, 10 steps, guidance 1.0 | 5.62 s | 2.94 s | **1.91x** | 109.7 to 73.4 s (1.49x) |
| base, 2 GPU CFG-parallel | 5.06 s | 2.84 s | 1.78x | 263.5 to 173.1 s (1.52x) |
| base, 2 GPU Ulysses SP=2 | 5.23 s | 3.08 s | 1.70x | 255.7 to 158.6 s (1.61x) |

Peak memory (base, 1 GPU, 1 clip), reserved / allocated: main 58.5 / 32.2 GB, PR 56.6 / 30.8 GB, PR with FP8 **27.2** / 23.7 GB. FP8 costs about 1-3% per step. Multi-clip and multi-GPU peak memory is about the same as main.

The FA3 path ran in every PR run: 0 flex autotune lines on a cold cache, while main logs them.

## Accuracy

- Unit tests (`test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py`): 47 passed on H100, 167 passed / 8 skipped (H100-only) on CPU. New tests cover:
  - split vs flex on H100: full and short clip, `log_scale` 0 and -1.3, FP8 on and off;
  - split vs dense masked attention on CPU, with a torch stand-in for FA3;
  - when the gate allows the split;
  - FP8 quantization: zero rows, outliers, saturation.
- Single attention call at the real shape, split vs flex: rel L2 3.6e-3, max abs 2.4e-4 (bf16 rounding).
- End to end, per-frame PSNR of the decoded video vs main. Main is bitwise deterministic across runs, so this measures the change:

  | setting | PSNR mean / worst frame |
  |---|---|
  | base, FP8 off | 39.0 / 36.0 dB |
  | base, FP8 on | 40.4 / 36.0 dB |
  | distilled | 40.2 / 37.8 dB |
  | 3 clips | 39.3, 36.8, 35.0 dB per clip / 30.5 dB |
  | 2 GPU CFG-parallel, SP=2 | 37.8 / 32.7 dB, 40.5 / 38.3 dB |

  FP8 adds no measurable error on top of the kernel change. The difference is bf16 rounding in a different attention kernel, compounded over steps and blocks. It grows across clips because each clip is conditioned on the previous one. Main itself moves 38-40 dB between 1 and 2 GPUs.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0c2e540-aef3-4e9e-9232-396e73d01fe1

![main vs this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/wan-animate2-refkv-assets/fa3/side_by_side.gif)

Multi-clip and multi-GPU videos, raw numbers, logs, profiler traces and harness scripts are in the comments below and in [the run archive](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/tree/wan-animate2-refkv-assets) ([INDEX.md](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/blob/wan-animate2-refkv-assets/INDEX.md)).

## Not covered

- TP > 1.
- Repeated runs for variance (all numbers are single runs).

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Benchmark and accuracy results

 # Eager flex_attention materializes the full [Q, KV] scores over the padded [gen | reference-video]
 # sequence (tens of GiB at video resolution); compiled, it is one fused kernel.
@@ -88,6 +89,51 @@ def _reference_video_key_mask(
     return key_mask
 
 
+def _pad_reference_video_kv(x: torch.Tensor, layout: _InContextLayout) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``[B, S_reference_video, H, D]`` -> this clip's reference frames in the zero-padded
+    per-frame-slot layout ``[B, reference_video_f * max_tokens_per_frame, H, D]`` that
+    _in_context_attention consumes, so the reference half of the flex K/V is one contiguous
+    copy per call. Sized to this clip, not the full clip, so a short clip's cache stays small."""
+    batch_size, _, num_heads, head_dim = x.shape
+    f = layout.reference_video_f
+    tokens_per_frame = layout.reference_video_tokens_per_frame
+    slot = layout.max_tokens_per_frame
+    out = x.new_zeros(batch_size, f * slot, num_heads, head_dim)
+    out.view(batch_size, f, slot, num_heads, head_dim)[:, :, :tokens_per_frame] = x[
+        :, : f * tokens_per_frame
+    ].view(batch_size, f, tokens_per_frame, num_heads, head_dim)
+    return out
+
+
+def _quantize_fp8_per_token_head(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """FP8 e4m3 with one fp32 scale per (batch, token, head): ``x ~= q * scale``, ``scale``
+    is ``[B, S, H, 1]``. All-zero rows (slot / SP padding) get scale 1 and stay exactly zero."""
+    fp8_max = torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn).max
+    x = x.float()
+    amax = x.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    scale = torch.where(amax > 0, amax / fp8_max, torch.ones_like(amax))
+    q = (x / scale).clamp_(-fp8_max, fp8_max).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    return q, scale
+
+
+def _split_attention_is_exact(q: torch.Tensor, layout: _InContextLayout) -> bool:
+    """Whether _split_in_context_attention reproduces the flex path exactly: generation and
+    reference frames both fill the slot, so the only zero-padded keys flex attends are the
+    missing frames of a short clip, which the split adds back as a softmax term. Grids that
+    differ by a row keep the flex path."""
+    return (
+        q.is_cuda
+        and q.shape[0] == 1
+        and current_platform.is_hopper()
+        and layout.generation_video_f >= 2
+        and layout.generation_video_tokens_per_frame == layout.max_tokens_per_frame
+        and layout.reference_video_tokens_per_frame == layout.max_tokens_per_frame
+        and layout.reference_video_f == layout.generation_video_f - 1
+    )
+
+

     """Wan block with the Wan-Animate-2 in-context self-attention.

+        v_scale_cache: dict[int, torch.Tensor] | None = None,

+            v_scale_cache[index] if v_scale_cache is not None else None,

@@ -311,10 +362,15 @@ def _in_context_attention(

         k: torch.Tensor,  # [B, seq_len, H, D] (gen-RoPE'd)
         v: torch.Tensor,  # [B, seq_len, H, D]
-        reference_video_k: torch.Tensor,  # [B, reference_video_seq_len, H, D] (reference-video RoPE'd)
-        reference_video_v: torch.Tensor,  # [B, reference_video_seq_len, H, D]
+        # [B, reference_video_f * max_tokens_per_frame, H, D] (reference-video RoPE'd), in the zero-padded
+        # slot layout of _pad_reference_video_kv; FP8 when the scales are given.
+        reference_video_k: torch.Tensor,
+        reference_video_v: torch.Tensor,
         block_mask: BlockMask,
         layout: _InContextLayout,
+        # [B, reference_video_f * max_tokens_per_frame, H, 1] fp32 when the reference K/V are FP8.

Multi-GPU results, 2x H100, base checkpoint, demo inputs, 40 steps, FP8 off. Full table is in the description.

| | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| CFG-parallel, denoise step | 5.06 s | 2.84 s | 1.78x |
| CFG-parallel, end to end | 263.5 s | 173.1 s | 1.52x |
| Ulysses SP=2, denoise step | 5.23 s | 3.08 s | 1.70x |
| Ulysses SP=2, end to end | 255.7 s | 158.6 s | 1.61x |

The FA3 path ran in both modes (0 flex autotune lines in the PR runs, 4 on main). PSNR vs main in the same mode is 37.8 dB (CFG) and 40.5 dB (SP). Main on 2 GPUs vs main on 1 GPU is in the same range, so the split adds no extra drift.
